answer: A new account is verified by a single-use code sent by post to one residential address, printed in ferrous ink and entered within fourteen days. The registrar matches the code against its ledger and rejects any second account at the same address, so a duplicate fails at registration instead of living on as a fable. Faking a thousand identities means renting a thousand mailboxes, while one honest person opens theirs once; a late code or a used address leaves it unverified, and the rejected count is published so the cost stays on the horizon.
